candidates.visible_reason: A round hole in the lower tie plate, on the field side away from the bolt head, shows no spike or fastener head. Only a brownish, wood-like surface and a small leaf fragment are visible inside it.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium. The hole is clearly visible, but a close-up of one plate cannot show whether this plate design uses a spike in every hole.
alternatives: unused or spare spike hole in the plate
alternate fastening design where the bolt-type fasteners hold the plate
spike removed during earlier maintenance and not an issue
wet or dark wood colour inside the hole

candidates.visible_reason: A round hole in the upper tie plate is filled with loose ballast stones and no spike head is visible. A second round hole on the same plate looks similar.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium to high. Debris could be covering a spike that sits lower, and the holes may be unused by design.
alternatives: ballast stones covering or filling a hole that is not used
alternate fastening design relying on the visible bolt heads
debris sitting above a spike that is seated below the plate surface

candidates.visible_reason: A rectangular notch or slot at the edge of the lower plate near the rail base is filled with leaf litter and dark debris. No fastener hardware is visible in it.
candidates.uncertainty: High. Slots like this are often part of the plate design and may never have held a fastener.

candidates.visible_reason: The exposed wood above the upper plate is grey-brown and weathered. Many lengthwise grain lines and splits run along it, and the surface looks rough and fibrous.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium to high. Surface checking is common on weathered timber, and this view cannot show how deep the splits go.
alternatives: normal surface weathering and shallow seasoning checks

candidates.visible_reason: The wood below the lower plate shows long vertical splits and a dark narrow gap or crack running along the grain, with a rough, worn surface.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium. A dark line could be a deep split or only a shadowed grain groove, and its depth cannot be judged from the image.
alternatives: ballast or debris lodged in a surface gap
